reason: A defect in deferral, found on 10 November 2026 from a website note (Shevchenko v Ruud, Stockholm R16, 11 November: 'Casper Ruud still in the draw of ongoing edition TML-2026-352'). The TennisIsMyLife ongoing file stopped updating on 5 November during the Paris Masters (it holds R64, R32 and seven of eight R16 matches, no final). The history assembly worked out who may still be playing from those files alone, so Ruud, who won his first two Paris matches there, counted as still in the Paris draw. ESPN then added the missing Paris results (Ruud lost the semi-final; the final was played), but espn.integrate only ADDED entries for editions with ESPN fixtures and never revised the earlier ones, so the stale entries survived. Two Stockholm R16 matches were held back for this reason in the local data at 10 November: Shevchenko v Ruud and Fritz v Norrie.
fix: history.assemble keeps the set of ongoing TML editions on the assembly (Assembly.ongoing_editions). espn.integrate works out who may still be playing again, once, over the history including the results it has just added, for the TML ongoing editions together with those that have ESPN fixtures, and REPLACES the earlier answer instead of adding to it. prospective.py gains the amendment mechanism the code rule names (accepted_code, amendments, amend) and evaluate counts forecasts whose code is the protocol's or a committed amendment's. Regression test: tests/test_forecast_espn.py IntegrateTests.test_who_is_still_playing_is_worked_out_again_with_the_results_espn_adds (fails on the frozen code, passes on this one).
features_unchanged: Yes. The ESPN results were already in the history that features are computed from, before and after the fix; the fix changes only Assembly.still_playing, which nothing but the deferral check (history.alive_elsewhere) reads. Feature definitions, profile settings and the replay are untouched.
models_unchanged: Yes. models/phase4_tournament_start.json and models/phase4_round_aware_r0.json are unchanged (same artifact hashes).
eligibility_unchanged: The rule is unchanged: a fixture is deferred while either player may still be playing an earlier-dated edition, and is forecast at a later run once that is no longer so. The fix makes the code apply that rule to the most complete history the run has, instead of to the TML files alone. What changes is that players whose earlier edition the history shows as finished for them (a recorded loss, or the edition's final) are no longer wrongly deferred, so some matches receive a forecast that the defect held back. A player genuinely still in an earlier edition is deferred as before.
outcomes_used: No. The defect was found from a deferral note on a match with no forecast; no P1 result or score was looked at to find or design the fix.
counting: forecasts carrying the previous fingerprint or this one count under the protocol's unchanged rules (first stored forecast, the same window, matches and metrics); stored forecasts are never changed. The amendment counts only once it is committed unchanged
